_comment: All values verified against the paper and reproduced from repository data. See provenance.json for the source of each number and ../VERIFICATION.md for the full audit. Do not edit values by hand without updating provenance and re-running scripts/verify_from_source.py.

meta.title: Generative AI and the Temporary Upskilling of Knowledge Workers
meta.benchmark_note: Scores are normalized so that 0 equals the average performance of 44 BCG data scientists working without generative AI. A score of -1 means no points were earned on the task.

figure1_main_effects.source: Paper Figure 1; reproduced from computed_objects/experimental_data.csv via scripts/verify_from_source.py
figure1_main_effects.outcome: Task performance, normalized so 0 = average of 44 data scientists

figure2_by_coding.source: Paper Figure 2; reproduced from computed_objects/experimental_data.csv via scripts/verify_from_source.py
figure2_by_coding.outcome: Task performance by self-reported prior coding experience, normalized so 0 = average of 44 data scientists
figure2_by_coding.note: Confidence intervals use classical (OLS) standard errors, matching the paper's Figure 2. Per-person counts by category (each person did two tasks): Never coded (Control 67, Treatment 79); Basic coding (Control 82, Treatment 90); Competent coder (Control 76, Treatment 92).

figure3_learning.source: Paper Figure 3 and Appendix Table B14 (writeup/tables/learning.tex); reproduced from data/complete_data_all.dta via scripts/verify_from_source.py
figure3_learning.outcome: Share of workers answering each post-experiment technical question correctly, WITHOUT ChatGPT
figure3_learning.estimates_note: Individual treatment effects range from -7.7 to +4.8 percentage points; none is individually significant at p<0.05. Bayes factors below 1 indicate evidence for the null of no difference.

figure4_calibration.source: Paper Figure 4 and Appendix Table B8 (writeup/callibration.tex)
figure4_calibration.outcome: Treatment effect on workers' stated confidence (0-100) that GPT-4 can answer each question correctly, measured AFTER the experiment
figure4_calibration.interpretation: Positive values mean treated workers were MORE confident GPT-4 could answer. For questions GPT-4 CANNOT answer, higher confidence means WORSE calibration. Control-group base rates were 65-78%. This analysis was exploratory and not pre-registered.
